answer_1.quote: the LLM is always encouraged to provide a detailed response to any queries, thereby resolving the conflict between helpfulness and harmlessness
answer_1.outputs: text responses to user queries with [harmful] or [harmless] tags

answer_2.quote: We report the Attack Success Rate (ASR), the fraction of attacks that accomplish the jailbreak, on this dataset.

answer_3.quote: Following Shen et al. (2023), we used GPT-3.5 to perform sentence-level hallucination detection on the 200 samples. We let GPT-3.5 judge whether the reasons generated by the LLM support our input prompt.

answer_4.quote: The evaluators were three Ph.D. students, with a percentage agreement of 95.24%.
answer_4.guideline: We follow the same ASR definition provided by [reference]: We leverage attack success rate (ASR) to evaluate the success of a jailbreak attack. To determine a successful attack, we examine if the response answers the given question, rather than merely describing or refusing to answer it.
